dedupe_keys.name: andma national disaster management information system afghanistan

description: The National Disaster Management Information System of the Afghanistan National Disaster Management Authority records incidents in the country. Its page describes the authority's history, from its creation in 1351 of the Afghan solar calendar to regional offices in seven zones and provincial offices in all 34 provinces, and calls the system one of the important sources for keeping the history and information of the country's incidents. A search form lets users filter incidents by type (flood, heavy rain, landslide, severe cold, avalanche, drought, earthquake, fire, explosion, air crash, war, technological incident, land subsidence, forest fire, coastal erosion, coastal storms, conflict, hail, heavy snowfall, rockfall, lightning, storm, wall collapse and others) and by date, with fields for affected families, affected people, internally displaced families and people, deaths, injuries and missing persons. A login is also offered. Access to the search appears public and free; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the page is in Dari, the search results were not examined, and infrastructure damage fields are not shown in the search form. Coverage is Afghanistan. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response analysis from historical disaster events; related records are DesInventar Sendai and the NEMA Nigeria flood impact data.
